field.label: Enabled
field.help: Send the scheduled reports and alerts. When disabled nothing is mailed, but previews still work.

field.label: Network name
field.help: Shown in the report heading and the mail subject.

field.label: Default recipients
field.help: Used by every schedule that has no recipients of its own. When empty, the mail account's own address is used.

field.label: Alert language
field.help: This is NOT the language of the reports. Each schedule carries its own, shown in the Language column on the Schedules tab, and a report only follows the system language when that schedule is set to System language. This field is the language of the instant alerts and the test message.

field.label: Mail server
field.help: Reuse the mail server already configured under Services: Monit, or enter a separate SMTP server.

field.label: SMTP port
field.help: Usually 465 for SSL/TLS or 587 for STARTTLS.

field.label: Authentication
field.help: Sign in to the SMTP server with the username and password below. Turn this off for a server that accepts mail without signing in.

field.label: Password
field.help: Stored on this firewall only. Leave empty to keep the current password.

field.label: Internet interface
field.help: Used for internet volume and the monthly data cap.

field.label: Local network
field.help: Devices on this network are listed in the report and watched for new arrivals.

field.label: VPN tunnels
field.help: Traffic and state of these tunnels are included in the report.

field.label: ntopng address
field.help: For the Applications section: the address of ntopng's web interface (os-ntopng). Empty: http://127.0.0.1:3000, ntopng on this firewall.

field.label: ntopng API token
field.help: Optional: a token made in ntopng for its REST API. With it, the Applications section shows ntopng's applications by traffic; without it, what Suricata recorded. Stored on this firewall only. Leave empty to keep the current token.

field.label: Send alerts
field.help: Send the alerts below as they happen, to every channel set here. Turned off, no alert is sent; the scheduled reports go on.

field.label: Alerts by mail
field.help: Mail the alerts to the default recipients, through the mail server above.

field.label: Webhook URL
field.help: Each alert is posted here as JSON: source, host, kind, at, subject, text and facts. The certificate is checked. Empty: no webhook.

field.label: Webhook header
field.help: Optional: one header line sent with each post, for example Authorization: Bearer followed by your token. Stored on this firewall only. Leave empty to keep the current header.

field.label: ntfy server
field.help: The address of an ntfy server, for example https://ntfy.example.com. There is no default: ntfy stays off until a server and a topic are set.

field.label: ntfy topic
field.help: The topic the alerts are published to. Anyone who knows the topic of a public server can read it: choose one that is hard to guess, or use an access token.

field.label: ntfy access token
field.help: Optional, sent as a bearer token. Stored on this firewall only. Leave empty to keep the current token.

field.label: Gateway down and back
field.help: Alert when a monitored gateway goes down and when it comes back, once the new state has held on two reads a minute apart. A gateway that changes state more than 3 times in 15 minutes gets one alert, and no more until it holds one state for 15 minutes.

field.label: Repeated failed logins
field.help: Alert when one address fails to sign in to the web GUI, the API or SSH this many times within 10 minutes, then nothing more for that address for 30 minutes. A failed API key is not counted: OPNsense logs no address for it.

field.label: Intrusion prevention alerts
field.help: Alert on Suricata alerts as they are logged: one alert per signature and source, then nothing more for that pair for 30 minutes.

field.label: VPN tunnels down and back
field.help: Alert when an IPsec, WireGuard or OpenVPN connection that has been up goes down, and when it comes back, with the same two reads as the gateways. A WireGuard peer counts as up while its last handshake is less than 3 minutes old.

field.label: Hardware watchdog reset
field.help: Alert once after a restart that the hardware watchdog caused, as os-watchdog records it.

field.label: Device reaching a command-and-control list
field.help: Alert the first time a device of the local networks tries to reach an address on a command-and-control list that os-blocklists blocks with its log on, and list the device in the report.

field.label: Alerts from other XGS plugins
field.help: Pass on the alerts that os-xgs-npu leaves for this plugin.

field.label: New device alert
field.help: Send a short message within five minutes when a device joins the local network for the first time.

field.label: Backup age warning (days)
field.help: Warn when the last remote configuration backup is older than this. 0 disables the check.

field.label: Monthly data cap (GB)
field.help: Download and upload together. Warns at 80% and 100%. 0 means unlimited.

field.label: Keep sent reports (days)
field.help: Copies of sent reports stay on the firewall for this many days and can be opened from the history tab. 0 keeps none.
